target.expr: "finished switching to system configuration" host:"$instance" | format "Deployed: <host>" as _msg | fields _time, _msg

list.name: Out of memory
list.titleFormat: Out of memory: a process was killed

panels.title: Cores
panels.description: Physical cores, and the threads they run: a core with hyper-threading runs two.

panels.title: Reporting
panels.description: How long ago it last sent data.

panels.title: Waiting
panels.description: The most time tasks spent waiting for CPU, memory or the disk (pressure). Sustained tens of percent means work is contending for the machine.

panels.title: Reporting, last 7 days
panels.description: Each hour a machine sent data is green; a gap is an hour it sent nothing (off, rebooting or cut off).

panels.title: Failed units
panels.description: systemd units failed now. Their lines are in the journal below; failures that have passed are on the Logs dashboard.

panels.title: Tailscale
panels.description: tailscaled's health warnings; `tailscale status` on the machine says what they are.

panels.title: Threads
panels.description: Each thread's CPU in use now, over the time shown; the two threads of a core share it.

targets.expr:
sort_by_label_numeric(
  label_replace(label_join(100 * (1 - rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{instance="$instance", mode="idle"}[$__rate_interval])) * on (instance, cpu) group_left (core) max by (instance, cpu, core) (last_over_time(node_cpu_info{instance="$instance"}[1h])), "thread", " · core ", "cpu", "core"), "thread", "cpu $1", "thread", "(.*)")
  or on (instance, cpu) label_replace(100 * (1 - rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{instance="$instance", mode="idle"}[$__rate_interval])), "thread", "cpu $1", "cpu", "(.*)"),
  "cpu")

panels.title: Core temperatures
panels.description: Each core's temperature now. Intel CPUs slow down near 100 °C.

targets.expr: sort_by_label_numeric(label_replace(max by (label) (node_hwmon_temp_celsius{instance="$instance", chip=~"platform_coretemp.*"} * on (instance, chip, sensor) group_left (label) node_hwmon_sensor_label{instance="$instance", chip=~"platform_coretemp.*", label=~"Core .*"}), "core", "core $1", "label", "Core (.*)"), "core")

panels.title: Clock and load
panels.description: The threads' average clock, and the load: tasks running or waiting, against the threads.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Used is what programs and VMs hold; cache is what the kernel gives back when it is needed; swap is zram, compressed in memory.

panels.title: Filesystems
panels.description: How full each filesystem is.

panels.title: Network
panels.description: The wired and wireless ports now; the top (over a minute) and the total over the time shown.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: CPU in use by kind, as a share of all threads.

panels.title: Waiting (pressure)
panels.description: The share of time some task waited for CPU, memory or the disk.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Used is what programs and VMs hold; the kernel gives cache back when it is needed. An orange mark is a process the kernel killed for memory.

panels.title: Load
panels.description: Tasks running or waiting; above the threads line, work queues.

panels.title: CPU per thread
panels.description: Each thread's CPU in use, from green (idle) to red (busy). The CPU chart is their average, so one thread at 100 % on a 12-thread machine shows there as 8 %; here it is a red row. Threads with the same core share it: when both are busy, each runs slower.

targets.expr:
sort_by_label_numeric(
  label_replace(label_join(100 * (1 - rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{instance="$instance", mode="idle"}[$__rate_interval])) * on (instance, cpu) group_left (core) max by (instance, cpu, core) (last_over_time(node_cpu_info{instance="$instance"}[1h])), "thread", " · core ", "cpu", "core"), "thread", "cpu $1", "thread", "(.*)")
  or on (instance, cpu) label_replace(100 * (1 - rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{instance="$instance", mode="idle"}[$__rate_interval])), "thread", "cpu $1", "cpu", "(.*)"),
  "cpu")

panels.title: Clock speed
panels.description: The threads' clock: their average, the fastest and the slowest, under the CPU's top speed (dashed). Idle threads slow down to save power; a busy machine whose fastest thread stays well under the top is held back, usually by heat (Temperatures, below) or its power limit.

panels.title: CPU by unit
panels.description: Each systemd unit's CPU, in threads' worth: 1 is one thread busy all the time. The 8 busiest, the rest as other, under the machine's threads. A user's sessions are one unit (user 1000); each yonder VM is its own.

panels.title: Memory by unit
panels.description: The memory each unit holds, not counting the file cache the kernel can take back. The 8 largest, the rest as other.

panels.title: Units
panels.description: Every unit now, busiest first: CPU in threads' worth over the last minute, and memory held.

panels.title: Wear
panels.description: The share of its rated writes the drive has used.

panels.title: Spare
panels.description: Spare blocks left for worn ones.

panels.title: Throughput
panels.description: Up is read, down is written.

panels.title: Latency
panels.description: The average time one read or write took. Empty while the disk is idle.

panels.title: Busy
panels.description: The share of time the disk had requests in flight.

panels.title: Network
panels.description: Physical interfaces; up is in, down is out.

panels.title: Tailscale
panels.description: Tailnet traffic by path: direct, or through a DERP relay (amber), which is slower. Up is in, down is out.

panels.title: VM traffic
panels.description: From each VM's TAP on its host: up is sent by the VMs, down is received. A VM is named by the end of its ID.

panels.title: VMs

targets.expr: max by (instance, device, vm) (label_replace(label_replace(node_systemd_unit_state{instance="$instance", state="active", name=~"yonder-vm-.*"} == 1, "vm", "$1", "name", "yonder-vm-(.*)\\.service"), "device", "yt-$1", "name", "yonder-vm-.*(.{12})\\.service"))

panels.description: Each VM, the machine it runs on, when it started, its CPU (threads' worth, over 5 minutes), the memory it holds, and its traffic.
